deep_dive.title: Opportunistic Conditional Entropy Coding with Frozen Analysis and Synthesis Transforms
deep_dive.abstract: In many delivery settings, a receiver may already hold a lower-quality or lower-resolution representation of an image, obtained through an independent transmission. Conventional codecs encode a subsequently requested higher-quality representation without exploiting this incidental side information, whereas conditional codecs generally assume a prescribed source of side information that is always available. We instead consider an opportunistic setting in which side information may or may not be present. We introduce a single entropy model that conditions on a previously decoded latent when available and falls back to a standard hyperprior otherwise. The proposed adapter maps the side-information latent to the prior signal required by the entropy model, allowing the same model to support multiple target and side-information quality combinations. The analysis and synthesis transforms remain frozen, enabling retrofitting of an existing learned codec while preserving its latent representation and reconstruction path. When the receiver holds the quality immediately below the target, the proposed method reduces the rate of the subsequent transmission by up to 46%, or by 52% when an additional hyper-latent is transmitted. In the absence of side information, the rate penalty remains below 4%, and the reconstructions are bit-identical across the conditional and fallback modes.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 论文针对传统编解码器在接收端已持有低质量或低分辨率图像时无法利用该附带边信息、而条件编解码器又假设边信息恒存在的问题，提出机会式条件熵编码方案。方法使用单一熵模型，在先前解码的隐变量可用时以其为条件，否则回退到标准超先验，并通过适配器把边信息隐变量映射为所需先验信号。结果表明确有边信息时压缩效率提升，无侧信息时性能仍保持稳定。该工作为条件熵编码与超先验结构设计提供了统一框架。

deep_dive.title: PULSE: Unlocking Practical Image Compression on Single-Thread CPU
deep_dive.abstract: Despite recent progress in learned image compression, existing methods remain computationally expensive on resource-constrained hardware, particularly CPUs. We introduce PULSE, a practical codec that enables (1) low-latency decoding on diverse hardware platforms with an ultra-low-complexity 5.2 kMAC/pixel neural receiver, and (2) efficient bit-exact entropy coding with an integer linear CDF predictor and a meta prior. To recover compression performance under this tight budget, we introduce an agentic evolution process guided by heuristic probes that iteratively improves the architecture through human-LLM collaboration. PULSE decodes a 1080p image in 126 ms on a single CPU thread while achieving compression performance comparable to HM. After perceptual optimization, PULSE competes with larger perceptual codecs like MS-ILLM. Codes are at https://github.com/microsoft/GenCodec/tree/main/PULSE

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Learned image compression remains too expensive for resource-constrained hardware, especially CPUs. PULSE combines an ultra-low-complexity 5.2 kMAC/pixel neural receiver, bit-exact entropy coding with an integer linear CDF predictor and meta prior, and an agentic evolution process that improves architecture via heuristic probes and human-LLM collaboration.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 学习式图像压缩虽进展显著，但在CPU等资源受限硬件上仍计算昂贵，难以实际部署。本文提出PULSE，一种实用编解码器：采用仅5.2 kMAC/像素的超低复杂度神经接收器实现低延迟解码，并用整数线性CDF预测器与元先验实现位精确熵编码。为在紧预算下恢复压缩性能，方法引入由启发式探针引导、人机协作的智能体演化流程迭代改进架构。实验显示单线程CPU解码1080p图像仅需126毫秒，压缩性能与HM相当，感知优化后进一步提升。
